title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
After Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder in order to stop the Profaned Flame, the city was burned down by a fire said to be coming from the sky, which burned only humans.

The only survivors of the Capital are the Handmaids, the court sorcerer Eamon, and the four malformed women. The Handmaids who served in the Capital reportedly took pleasure in hurting others.

Sometime after the Profaned Flame destroyed the Capital, Pontiff Sulyvahn discovered the Profaned Flame and the Capital, "a burning ambition took root within him". He would later infuse the Profaned Flame within his own greatsword, and would perhaps introduce the Profaned Flame to the Fire Witches. They would learn to use its power and summon firestorms with their halberds., and would eventually take Irithyll for themselves.

Sulyvahn would later build a dungeon, and hired some handmaids to guard the prison, which preserves part of the profaned flame in a icy skull.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Yhorm the Giant -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Yhorm, normally spelled Jorm, is an Old Norse word meaning "huge". It appears in the name of the Norse world-serpent *Jormungandr*, literally "huge monster". The spelling Yhorm may help with pronunciation, as the letter J is usually pronounced in Old Norse as a Y.
His appearance seems unique to giants. For one he is the only living giant with facial features, consisting of two bright red eyes and an angular jawline. His proportions are very similar to human proportions, unlike most giants in the games, and he appears to be taller than the giants of Anor Londo.
A player version of Yhorm's armor set exists in the game files, but it is not available to the player under normal circumstances.
Despite being one of the easiest bosses to beat, Yhorm has the highest HP of any boss in *Dark Souls III* (including Darkeater Midir, Sister Friede, and The Demon Prince).

title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: After the end of the great war, Lord Gwyn and his clan gained dominion over the world and began their Age of Fire, with the giants continuing to coexist with their civilization in a subordinate but close position. A number of giants became Sentinels guarding the walls and streets of Anor Londo, the city of the gods, employing giant halberds made of brass and retaining the power of lightning, giant shields of white iron, and heavy armor of finely decorated golden brass. An even more powerful group of giants defended the royal cathedral in the center of the city and were capable of performing restorative and offensive miracles.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: One day, when Sulyvahn was still young, he unearthed the Profaned Capital underneath the outskirts of Irithyll; he also discovered in the ruins of the city the Profaned Flame. It was a "cold" flame, found preserved in icy remains; it was an unfading, everlasting flame, and one that held within it the Dark of humanity. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Yhorm refused to serve as fuel for the First Flame a second time due to the fact that, once awakened from his grave, he realized that his sacrifice had been futile. The sorcerers of the Profaned Capital had continued to experiment on the Profaned Flame he had tried to quell with his sacrifice and as a result the entire city was destroyed, making his life of service meaningless even after the end. The moment he rises from the grave, he can be seen already howling in despair. In addition, he may also have simply understood the state of the world, now corrupted beyond any possibility of traditional salvation through the linking of the Fire, and simply decided to await death in the ruins of his city.

snippet: It is possible to theorize that the event in which the Profaned Flame went out of control, destroying the Profaned Capital, was the result of a Court Sorcerers ritual gone awry. In fact, these sorcerers did not care about their creations even when they were as dangerous as the dark flame, continuing to live as if nothing had happened, driven by an unethical and unruly pursuit of knowledge. In addition, the only survivors of the destruction of the city are a noble court sorcerer and the handmaids, possibly in the noble's service, implying that someone had somehow managed to avoid being devoured by the flame. Furthermore, the detail of the Profaned Flame "falling" from the sky and devouring only human beings implies an unnatural event in which the flame was not in its previous controlled conditions but was activated toward human targets.

title: Yhorm's Greatshield
snippet:
Yhorm's Greatshield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Yhorm's Greatshield is on the heavier end of greatshields, being in the same weight class as titans like the Moaning Shield and Stone Greatshield.

What makes it unique among greatshields, however, is that it increases the player's Poise by 15% while wielded, a trait shared only by the Lothric Knight Long Spear. As such, it pairs well with large Hyper Armor weapons, allowing the wielder to more easily win trades against foes foolish enough to engage.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : At the beginning of the fight, charge at Aldrich to avoid his hard-hitting soul spear. Get behind him and focus your attacks on his tail. If the arrows following the player catch up to them, then that player will most likely go down quick. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended for this fight.

Casting the sorcery Twisted Wall of Light can negate Aldrich's ranged attacks, including his arrow barrage in the second phase, allowing one to wait out the attack by casting repeatedly.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At one point, Sulyvahn sent McDonnell, an Archdeacon from Irithyll that was a sorcerer despite being a high-ranking cleric, to help the deacons of the Cathedral. McDonnell shared his sorceries with the priests of the Cathedral, who in turn became sorcerers, turning their holy candles into sorcery staves and blades, better equipped to face the abominations of the Deep. However McDonnell would soon find delight in the stagnant souls of the Deep, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world". Over time the deacons themselves, despite their faith and holy flame, began to succumb to the power of the Deep. They began to add dark stories about the Deep to the holy scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and by studying it, he created sorceries that manipulated the dark soul dregs, then imparted them to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons.

The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

Instead, the Ashen One merely sits beside the flame, unable to prolong its life, as the sun remains a Darksign.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
After killing Oceiros, the Ashen One acquires the means to access two more optional areas. One is a gesture that will allow passage to Archdragon Peak, and the other is a secret path to the Untended Graves, a dark version of Firelink Shrine. Here the Ashen One finds Champion Gundyr, and behind him an abandoned Firelink Shrine home only to a Shrine Handmaiden. Here the Ashen One can find the Eyes of a Fire Keeper which if presented to the Firekeeper will allow her to see a dark vision of the future that the Ashen One may choose to fulfill.

In Archdragon Peak, the Ashen One can face the Ancient Wyvern and The Nameless King, once known as Lord Gwyn's Firstborn, the old God of War who aligned himself with the Ancient Dragons.

title: Ashen One
snippet: After defeating Halflight, the path to Filianore is open. Filianore lies sleeping while clutching a broken egg-like object. If the Ashen One touches the object, it will shatter into pieces and Filianore will wake, upon which a blinding light emanates from the shards of the object and envelopes the chamber. The Ashen One opens their eyes to find that the Ringed City is now a lifeless desert, and Filianore an emaciated corpse. Leaving her room, the Ashen One comes upon a fleeing Pygmy. Investigating the scene closer, they find Gael consuming the remains of a Pygmy Lord in order to gain their Dark Soul. He proceeds to attack the Ashen One in order to gain their piece of the Dark Soul.

 cemetery_of_ash : At some point in time, the Ashen One attempted to link the fire. They were not powerful enough and were instead burnt to ash by the flames. Some time later, the Ashen One was awakened by the toll of the bells in the Cemetery of Ash, signifying that the link of fire was threatened. The Ashen One emerges from their grave and sets out to leave their tomb. Finding the Coiled Sword lodged inside Iudex Gundyr, the Ashen One pulls it out, awakening Gundyr and beginning a fight. Halfway through, Gundyr is seemingly consumed by the Pus of Man, but the Ashen One defeats him and finds Firelink Shrine.

 catacombs_of_carthus : Progressing through the trap-ridden Catacombs, the Ashen One eventually finds a rickety drawbridge that will lead them to Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Should the Ashen One choose to descend the fallen drawbridge, they may find the Smouldering Lake, ruled by the Old Demon King and home to various demons and a great slithering worm.

Across the bridge, the Ashen One finds a strange goblet that pulls them into the Abyss. Here they encounter High Lord Wolnir, who attacks the Ashen One. By destroying his enchanted bracelets, Wolnir loses his grip and falls into the Abyss, allowing the Ashen One to return to the regular world, where the path to Irithyll, a frozen city guarded by an impenetrable barrier and ruled by Pontiff Sulyvahn in the name of Aldrich, is now open.

title: Ashen One

After returning to Firelink Shrine, the Ashen One again encounters Anri and Horace, who tell the Ashen One that Aldrich supposedly hails from Irithyll and that he may have returned home. They will also find Sirris of the Sunless Realms, who shows little interest in the Ashen One, unless they provide the Handmaiden with a certain ash, prompting Sirris to offer the Ashen One her sign.

 soul_of_cinder : After returning to the shrine, the Ashen One places the ashes of the Lords on their thrones, and the Firekeeper channels their strength to the Ashen One. The Firekeeper bids the Ashen One travel to the First Flame. Accepting the strength of the Lords, the Ashen One is transported to a copy of the Firelink shrine, standing amid the wreckage of kingdoms. From there, the Ashen One proceeds to the Kiln of the First Flame.

There they encounter the Soul of Cinder, a manifestation of the Lords that had previously linked the flame. The Soul of Cinder takes on many forms and fighting styles, mimicking those who had linked the flame. Once the Ashen One weakens it, the Soul of Cinder assumes the style of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, first one to link the flame. After defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One is presented with four options depending on the choices they made.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
***Ash Seeketh Embers**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. Before the flames fade, the Ashen One may strike her down. The Ashen One steps over the limp body of the Fire Keeper and takes the First Flame into their own hands. Kneeling, the Ashen One raises the flame, offering it to the Darksign Sun.
***The Usurpation of Fire**: If the Ashen One allowed Yoel to draw out their true strength a sufficient amount of times through the Dark Sigil, followed Yuria's instructions and "married" Anri, the Ashen One may, instead of linking the fire, absorb it into themselves. The Ashen One collapses from the strain and awakens before a Darksign Sun turned white, and also finds Yuria, Anri, and an army of hollows greeting them as their Lord and praying for the Ashen One to make Londor whole.

Anri seeks Aldrich, and thinks to find him in the Cathedral of the Deep. They offer their help to the Ashen One, should the Ashen One need it. Here the Ashen One may also find Orbeck of Vinheim, a sorcerer who will offer to share his knowledge if the Ashen One brings him magic scrolls.

Making their way through the Crucifixion Woods leads the Ashen One to a crossroads. One path leads to Farron Keep, home of the Abyss Watchers, whereas the other one, guarded by one of the Crystal Sages, leads to the Cathedral of the Deep, home of Aldrich.

 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

Upon encountering the Ashen One, Yoel offers his services, providing rudimentary sorceries and offering to draw out the Ashen One's "true strength", not telling them that doing so will burden the Ashen One with the Dark Sigil which will make them hollow upon death.

Inside the Settlement, the Ashen One is accosted by the inhabitants of the town and pelted with massive arrows by a Giant atop a tower. The Ashen One fights their way through the Archives, and find themselves close to the location of Prince Lothric, who hides at the very top of the castle. Lothric has no intention of returning as a Lord of Cinder however, preferring to watch the world end from afar with his brother Lorian. The brothers attack the Ashen One, who slays them both, and claims Lothric's ashes.

title: Court Sorcerer Eamon
snippet:
Court Sorcerer Eamon -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Court Sorcerer Eamon is a very aggressive opponent. He awaits on the roof of the ruined chapel in the Profaned Capital. Due to the area's layout, he will most likely approach from the rear while the player is making their way upstairs; this usually gives him the opportunity to start the battle by casting one of his sorceries. His repertoire includes Soul Spear and Homing Soulmass.

He also comes armed with a Gargoyle Flame Hammer and will quickly switch between casting spells and this weapon, frequently holding it with both hands for increased damage. His melee attacks are very similar to that of Havel's, and thus he is often vulnerable after finishing a combo. Care must be taken, though, as he can quickly inflict a considerable amount of damage in return; more so if the player is taken off-balance due to the different tactics used for dealing with a sorcerer and a warrior.
